name: Whipped Cream No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: coffeecupfuls of good thick sweet cream
ingredients.originalText: three coffeecupfuls of good thick sweet cream

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a cup of powdered sugar

ingredients.name: three-fourths of an ounce of best gelatine
ingredients.originalText: three-fourths of an ounce of best gelatine

instructions.text: Whip three coffeecupfuls of good thick sweet cream with half a cup of powdered sugar and three teaspoonfuls of vanilla to a stiff froth
Dissolve three-fourths of an ounce of best gelatine in a teacup of hot water
When cool pour it in the cream and stir it gently from the bottom upward, cutting the cream into it, until it thickens
The dish which contains the cream should be set in another dish containing ice-water, or cracked ice
When finished pour in molds and set on ice or in any very cold place

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Whip three coffeecupfuls of good thick sweet cream with half a cup of powdered sugar and three teaspoonfuls of vanilla to a stiff froth
2. Dissolve three-fourths of an ounce of best gelatine in a teacup of hot water
3. When cool pour it in the cream and stir it gently from the bottom upward, cutting the cream into it, until it thickens
4. The dish which contains the cream should be set in another dish containing ice-water, or cracked ice
5. When finished pour in molds and set on ice or in any very cold place
